what: Two published known answers for SplitMix64, the word generator under the noise source.
how: Not produced by this project. They are the answers the Rosetta Code task 'Pseudo-random numbers/Splitmix64' states: https://rosettacode.org/wiki/Pseudo-random_numbers/Splitmix64 , a page that says it was last edited on 6 November 2026, read on 2026-11-23. The limit of that read: it was made with a tool that hands back a small model's rendering of the page, not the page's bytes, and the reader had recalled all ten figures before asking. Both answers are also reproduced by tests/test_mod_a_reference.py with numpy's uint64 arithmetic, which imports nothing of model/.

first_words.why: the first five 64-bit words for the seed 1234567

counts.why: for the seed 987654321, how many of the first 100,000 words fall in each fifth of the range: bin = floor(word * 5 / 2^64)
